subject: Proposal: Indexing & Cold-Storage Partner Co-sell Framework
body:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Patel <amit@pinecone.io>, Sofie Berg <sofie@weaviate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Indexing & Cold-Storage Partner Co-sell Framework

Hi Amit and Sofie,

Thanks again for the quick sync last week — great to get Pinecone and Weaviate perspectives on hybrid vector storage and the push / pull between hot indexes and S3-backed cold stores. Marissa and Laura are looped in to help map GTM and technical handoffs.

Why I’m writing: we want to propose a concise co-sell framework that covers three things: 1) a joint POC scope that shows sub-100ms retrieval on hot queries while transparently falling back to S3 for cold vectors, 2) a commercial split and lead-routing mechanism, and 3) a joint enablement package for partners and pilot customers.

High-level draft (details attached):
- POC scope (2–4 weeks): small production dataset (50–200k vectors), Redwood-hosted model routing + inference, Pinecone/Weaviate as primary index, S3 as cold-tier with on-demand rehydration.
- Success metrics: 95th pct latency < 200ms for hot queries, cold-tier retrieval within < 2s for rehydrated results, and < 20% query fallthrough to cold after warmup.
- Responsibilities: Pinecone/Weaviate handle indexing+serve; Redwood handles model routing, prefix/KV cache, and evaluation harness; CloudEdge handles integration labor for select pilots.
- Commercial & co-sell: joint case studies, shared webinar, and a simple MQL routing rule in HubSpot (ref link below).

Attachments: indexing-cold-storage-co-sell-matrix.xlsx (commercial splits + checklist), poc-scope-architecture-diagram.png (sequence flow), draft-co-sell-terms-v1.docx (legal stub).

Can you both confirm high-level alignment and surface any must-have technical constraints (e.g., preferred ingestion formats, TTL on vectors, or specific S3 lifecycle rules you require)? If this looks reasonable I’ll turn it into a short SOW and a one-page press-ready blurb.

Thanks,
Jonas
--
Jonas Weber
Partner Strategy | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

-----Original Message-----
From: Amit Patel <amit@pinecone.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Sofie Berg <sofie@weaviate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Indexing & Cold-Storage Partner Co-sell Framework

Jonas — thanks for the thoughtful draft. Pinecone is aligned on the idea of a hybrid offering; a couple of notes from our side: 

1) Ingestion format: we prefer batched upserts in ndjson with base64-encoded vector payloads for a clean pipeline. We can accept CSV for small pilots but recommend ndjson for production.
2) Cold retrieval design: we’d like to avoid synchronous blocking on S3 on high-QPS endpoints. Recommended pattern: return a cached placeholder, kick async rehydrate, and surface the rehydrated candidate in a follow-up event (we can demo within the POC).
3) Legal/commercial: we can support joint case studies but require Pinecone approval on any customer quotes. The commercial split matrix in your sheet looks fair; would like to propose a simplified alternative: 60/30/10 (Redwood/Pinecone/CloudEdge) for incremental revenue from joint pilots if we bring the customer.

I’ve attached a short note (inline below) with a sample ingestion snippet and a link to our SDK. Happy to run a short tech deep-dive with your infra team next week.

—Amit

> Sample upsert (pseudo):
> curl -X POST https://controller.pinecone.io/vectors/upsert 
> -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
> -d '{"vectors": [{"id":"doc-1","values":"<base64>"}]}'

-----Original Message-----
From: Sofie Berg <sofie@weaviate.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Amit Patel <amit@pinecone.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Indexing & Cold-Storage Partner Co-sell Framework

Hi Jonas and Amit — thanks, this is a strong starting point. A few Weaviate-specific constraints to call out: 

- Vector TTL & snapshots: we recommend a nightly snapshot export to S3 (avro/parquet) for disaster recovery and to make cold retrieval deterministic.
- Hybrid queries: Weaviate supports chaining a search that hits local index + a fallback pipeline; we propose adding a small re-rank step inside Redwood so that the ranking model can rescore rehydrated candidates consistently.
- Operational footprint: our team can provide a managed connector that handles incremental sync and snapshotting; we charge a setup fee for pilot connectors but can waive it for a co-sell reference customer.

Also attaching a short checklist for pilot readiness (I referenced a few items inline in the attached matrix). Happy to refine the SOW language — I’ll be on the call Thurs 09/03 11:00 PT if you want to walk through line-by-line.

Best,
Sofie

Subject: Re: Proposal: Indexing & Cold-Storage Partner Co-sell Framework

Thanks both — useful notes. Quick summary and requested next steps for this thread: 

- Tech: Pinecone will lead on live ingest format and async rehydrate pattern; Weaviate will provide snapshot-to-S3 guidance and managed connector for incremental sync. Redwood will own the unified routing layer, re-rank hook, and POC evaluation harness.
- Commercial: accept the 60/30/10 split for pilot-sourced revenue (Amit, confirm you’re ok with the 60/30/10 if Redwood sources the lead). Marissa to draft a co-sell one-pager and an abbreviated SOW.
- Logistics: Laura to schedule the joint tech session (Thursday 09/03 11:00 PT) and create a HubSpot deal (link below).

If everyone confirms I’ll send the SOW and calendar invites and we’ll move to the pilot phase.

Jonas
